rules: Backlog is required before meaningful implementation.
Every meaningful code, docs, extension, or workflow change must map to an issue_id.
Builder may reason, but must not modify files without explicit human approval.
QA and validation must be deterministic whenever possible.
Project-specific memory must live in the target project, not globally in Kajiya Build Line.

items.title: Define project vision, backlog, and handoff protocol
items.problem: The repository exists and has an initial Pi extension, but it needs a canonical objective, backlog, and handoff protocol so work can resume without relying on chat memory.
items.expected_behavior: A new session can read README.md, docs/state/backlog.json, docs/state/current-project.json, and docs/LLM_HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md to understand the project and next safe actions.
close_criteria: README explains the project purpose and relationship to Kajiya Context Engine.
Backlog exists and includes initial KBL issues.

items.title: Formalize kajiya_onboard_project as the first read-only pi.dev
items.problem: The local Pi extension can inject an onboarding prompt, but the onboarding station needs to be formalized as the first permanent pi.dev-style step.
items.expected_behavior: Running /kajiya-onboard in Pi starts a read-only project discovery step that inspects the current repo and returns JSON-compatible readiness output.
close_criteria: The onboarding prompt does not assume any specific project.

items.title: Add project profile initialization with explicit confirmation
items.problem: Kajiya Build Line needs a way to initialize project-local identity without contaminating global memory.
items.expected_behavior: A confirmed init step creates .kajiya/project.json with project-local paths, validation commands, memory policy, and external write policy.
close_criteria: Generated profile contains no machine-specific secrets.

items.title: Add deterministic status and QA commands
items.problem: The build line needs deterministic checks before and after Builder-assisted work.
items.expected_behavior: Commands can inspect git status, compile Python sources, check expected files, and report JSON without LLM reasoning.
close_criteria: Status works from an external git repo.

items.title: Design Builder as bounded Pi/Pocock reasoning step
items.problem: The project needs a Builder step that uses Pi/Pocock's configured model without adding a separate Gemini SDK client.
items.expected_behavior: The Builder receives a selected issue_id and local evidence, then returns a structured patch plan without modifying files.
close_criteria: Builder does not run before backlog issue selection.
Builder does not use Gemini SDK directly.
Builder cannot claim files changed unless a deterministic step changed them.

items.title: Add deterministic issue transition and close command
items.problem: Issue closure and workstream transitions are currently performed with long ad-hoc Python snippets pasted into the terminal, which is not replicable or aligned with Kajiya Build Line.
items.expected_behavior: A deterministic command can close one backlog issue, attach evidence, activate the next issue, update current-project state, and return JSON-compatible output.
close_criteria: A backlog issue can be closed without a custom pasted Python script.
The next issue can be activated deterministically.
Evidence paths can be attached to the closed issue.
